notes.title: Pulling the plug
notes.notes: [p]Hey! It's the creator guy! Although I'm sure I am talking into the void, considering the unfortunately small playerbase and inconsistency of development, I am sad to say that I am going to pull the plug on Dynamite Joe vs The Deep Sea Invasion/ENEMIES GONE SUBURBAN[/p][p][/p][p]It's been a long time coming. I have made some big mistakes in the development of the game that I regret. Having a full do-over over I would have kept ENEMIES GONE SUBURBAN's original concept rather than attempting a story mode like the other ENEMIES games and would have kept in exclusively arcade in it's theme. Not something to change your life, just to entertain you for a couple of hours and have a good time. [/p][p][/p][p]At the end of the day, I was very unclear on my goal with the project and couldn't ever figure out what scale was achievable, as I am just one guy, not a team that could make a vast character-rich world with quirky guns, clever enemies, and a smashing soundtrack. That has and will always be by biggest enemy when making games like these. On top of that, I already work a 50-hour/week day job, and there is simply no time.[/p][p][/p][p]If there was a lesson learned, it would be to be more realistic about scale and focus on making something small and great rather than something with AAA scale with 0.0000001% of the time and budget.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]I would absolutely love to revisit the idea of fighting off enemies in a round-by-round fast fast-paced shoot 'em' up with modular guns and all that jazz. Today is not the day that happens or honestly for a while.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p]Peace out,[/p][p][/p][p]-Jumbo[/p]

notes.title: Getting Fishy Wit' it
notes.notes: Depreciated old Gone Suburban mode and have fully migrated to the new Dynamite Joe concept including fleshed-out short story mode and more to come down the road (slowly but surely)

notes.title: Big changes coming...
notes.notes:
ENEMIES GONE SUBURBAN was awesome while it lasted! After a month on standby getting nothing done on the development side I decided I didn't know what I wanted from the project and was happy with what I created but making another addition to the enemies franchise that hadn't exactly found the audience I wanted it to... I'm deciding to go in a different direction with this project and it will now be...



[i]Drum roll, please[/i]



[i][b]Dynamite Joe Vs The Deep Sea Invasion![/b][/i]


The core of the old game will be kept but I'm gonna change it to a linear shorter story and really focus on that quality vs quantity aspect and just try and deliver a game that's exciting, fresh, and new from what I've been doing since 2019

Think it's time to pull the plug on the ENEMIES franchise and start branching out to more solo projects and see where that takes me :-)

notes.title: Game Roadmap Updates!
notes.notes:
Hey there casual gamer! I trust you're doing well on this fine day. 

With that out the way boy do we have some news for you!

So as I've been working on ENEMIES: GONE SUBURBAN over the past year I've stirred up more interest to pursue this project so something I considered a "simple break from the norm" and a game title I didn't intend to be more than just a little free to play survival game to tide the average gamer over for a half hour or so has now shown more promise so I'm gonna be making these following changes with the release...


[b]CAMPAIGN[/b]

[b]PAID GAME[/b]


Now I know the bold text can make those two things intimating but...wait! They are in fact intimating!

I want to put more love and care into this game, flesh it out, see where it goes, learn some shit, and get messy!


My goal is to release within the year for around $10.00-$15.00 with a full campaign, tons of new weapons and ways to play, and above all very very satisfying gunplay


-The creator dude
